dockerhub:alpine.why: alpine releases in 3.x branches (3.23, 3.24), each its own package set and support window

dockerhub:arangodb.why: arangodb numbers its release lines 3.x (3.11, 3.12), and a 3.x move changes the storage engine defaults

dockerhub:caddy.why: caddy 2 is semver: a 2.x minor keeps the Caddyfile and API compatible

dockerhub:cassandra.why: cassandra numbers its release lines x.y (4.0, 4.1, 5.0), each with its own sstable format and support window

dockerhub:codercom/code-server.why: code-server keeps major 4 and moves its minor with each monthly VS Code release, so a 4.x minor is a routine step on one line

dockerhub:clickhouse/clickhouse-server.why: clickhouse numbers its releases YY.M (24.3, 24.8), each a release line with its own settings changes

dockerhub:collabora/code.why: collabora numbers its releases YY.MM (25.04, 26.04), and the parts after that are builds of one release

dockerhub:couchdb.why: couchdb is semver: a 3.x minor keeps the data and HTTP API compatible

dockerhub:dpage/pgadmin4.why: pgadmin4 ships a 9.x minor every month as a routine release; only the leading number is a line

dockerhub:elasticsearch.why: elasticsearch is semver: the index format and settings change on the leading number

dockerhub:golang.why: Go numbers its release lines 1.x (1.26, 1.27), each with its own language and toolchain changes

dockerhub:influxdb.why: influxdb is semver: a 2.x minor keeps the data and API compatible

dockerhub:kibana.why: kibana is semver and moves with elasticsearch on the leading number

dockerhub:mariadb.why: mariadb numbers its release series x.y (10.11, 11.4), each run through mariadb-upgrade

dockerhub:mysql.why: mysql numbers its release lines x.y (8.0, 8.4 LTS, 9.x innovation), each upgrading the data dictionary

dockerhub:neo4j.why: neo4j numbers its lines by the leading number (5, then calendar years 2025, 2026)

dockerhub:nginx.why: nginx numbers its branches 1.x (an odd mainline, an even stable), and the leading 1 never moves

dockerhub:node.why: node numbers its release lines by the leading number (24, 26)

dockerhub:nvidia/cuda.why: CUDA numbers its toolkit releases x.y (13.0, 13.5), each with its own runtime libraries and driver floor

dockerhub:otel/opentelemetry-collector-c.why: the collector is 0.x, where every minor is a release that can rename or drop config keys

dockerhub:percona.why: percona server follows the mysql release lines x.y (8.0, 8.4), each upgrading the data dictionary

dockerhub:postgres.why: postgres numbers its majors by the leading number (16, 17, 18)

dockerhub:python.why: python numbers its feature releases 3.x (3.13, 3.14), each with its own C API and removals

dockerhub:rabbitmq.why: rabbitmq numbers its release series x.y (3.13, 4.0, 4.1), each with its own feature flags

dockerhub:redis.why: redis is semver: the RDB format moves on the leading number

dockerhub:solr.why: solr is semver: the index format moves on the leading number

dockerhub:traefik.why: traefik numbers its releases v3.x, and a minor adds and deprecates providers and options

dockerhub:ubuntu.why: ubuntu numbers its releases YY.MM (24.04, 26.04), each its own distribution
